species.real: Sphagnum builds its own bog: it soaks up nutrients and gives off acid, making the ground too sour and soggy for most rival plants, and it comes in red, green and gold depending on the species.
species.name: Dubhlet

dex.text: A small cushion of moss in red, green and gold, with a black peaty pool where its back should be. Tread on one and it makes a noise like a wet sponge sighing.
dex.fact: Dubh is Gaelic for black: the dubh lochans of the Flow Country are small pools of dark water stained by peat, and they are home to dragonflies, water beetles and nesting waders.

species.real: In the 1980s tax breaks let wealthy investors, celebrities among them, plant conifers on the Flow Country; the outcry helped end the scheme in 1988, and many of the trees are now being felled to restore the bog.
species.name: Flowmoor

dex.text: A great slow blanket of living moss with dark pools winking in its back. It has been growing for about ten thousand years and sees no reason to hurry now.
dex.fact: The Flow Country of Caithness and Sutherland is the largest expanse of blanket bog in Europe. In 2024 it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the first peatland to be listed, and its peat holds a vast store of carbon.
